evidence.excerpt:
Scientific discovery requires ideas that are original, useful, and non-obvious. Yet AI scientists are typically
given as much task information as possible during idea generation, which can anchor generation toward
familiar approaches. Inspired by the cognitive framework ofBlind VariationandSelective Retention
(BVSR), we propose a discovery framework that separates these two roles of information: it generates
proposals under deliberately limited task information to broaden exploration, then learns from proposals
previously verified on the same task and their outcomes to retain promising candidates for costly empirical
evaluation. We evaluate BVSR across five proposer models and 12 scientific tasks. Limiting task information
substantially increases proposal originality and non-obviousness, and produces a larger share of highly
creative and high-utility proposals than existing

Prior work improves AI-scientist creativity by modifying prompt instructions. We compare against
three such baselines: analogical reasoning, cross-domain search, and no-domain search [ 37]. We
further add one control: BV with the full task description, which separates the effect of limited
information from that of our prompt. All methods share the same proposer models, candidate
budget, and reasoning configuration. For each model and task, we generate 112 proposals and
report in Table 1 the top creativity and top utility, defined here as the mean creativity and utility of
the top 1% of proposals, together with mean originality and mean non-obviousness.
Table 1. Comparison of BV with baselines.The highest is shown in bold. Values are mean±SE.

training set. We also compare withSFTusing the same backbone, trained with mean-squared error.
Findings.Figure 3 shows that learned SR preserves top candidates much more effectively than
prompting-based screeners. The in-context learning baseline, despite seeing verified outcomes of
similar proposals, performs no significantly better than zero-shot judges. SFT improves preservation
over many prompt-based methods. Nevertheless, it remains less effective than SR. This result is
consistent with the motivation that accurate prediction throughout the distribution is a different
objective from keeping exceptional candidates out of the discard set. At a discard ratio of 50%, SR
preserves 79% of the top-5% proposals by creativity and 82% of the top-5% proposals by utility. We
therefore use this SR model to discard the lowest-ranked 50% of proposals in later experiments.

preserves 79% of the top-5% proposals by creativity and 82% of the top-5% proposals by utility. We
therefore use this SR model to discard the lowest-ranked 50% of proposals in later experiments.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Blinded human expert assessments validate the LLM-based semantic grouping for originality and confirm a statistically significant non-obviousness advantage for BV proposals over the analogical reasoning baseline.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective benchmark task metrics (e.g., Kendall correlation, AUROC, held-out R2, negative MAE) computed on executed candidate programs, plus blinded PhD-level human expert ratings for originality and non-obviousness.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Verified empirical utility scores from previously executed proposals, used to train the pairwise selective retention ranking model.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims that BV improves proposal creativity and that SR retains top proposals while reducing evaluation cost are well supported by the experimental data and figures. Full-system integration with SimpleTES shows consistent end-to-end gains across all tested discovery domains.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation spans 12 discovery tasks across biology, astrodynamics, ML, and neuroscience using 5 proposer LLMs, supported by objective task metrics (e.g., Kendall tau, AUROC, R2, MAE) and ablation studies. Automatic evaluations of originality and non-obviousness are corroborated by blinded human expert validation exhibiting high agreement and statistically significant correlation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Blinded PhD-level human expert assessments validate semantic clustering for originality and confirm statistically significant gains in non-obviousness for BV proposals over baselines.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective ground-truth benchmark metrics (e.g., Kendall correlation, AUROC, held-out R2, negative MAE) run on test task executions, as well as blinded human expert ratings.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Historical candidate execution utility scores used to train the pairwise selective retention ranking model.

primary.limitations: The work acknowledges computational requirements of running verified code evaluations, reliance on small dense models for V-usable information estimation, and dependence on LLMs for semantic grouping during large-scale scoring.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, formulating creativity through Simonton's three-criterion metric (originality, utility, non-obviousness) and quantifying context information via V-usable information. The blind variation stage uses controlled information-limited contexts, while selective retention trains a scalar scoring head on pairwise utility preferences between top-5% and remainder candidates.
primary.quality_rationale: The study presents a clear, theoretically motivated, and experimentally robust contribution to AI-driven scientific discovery. The combination of objective programmatic benchmarks, rigorous baseline comparisons, comprehensive ablations, and blinded human expert validation meets the standard for curated acceptance.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Blind Variation and Selective Retention (BVSR) for automated scientific discovery, showing that limiting task information during ideation increases proposal originality/non-obviousness and that training a pairwise ranking selector on verified empirical outcomes safely filters unpromising proposals.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study presents a clear, theoretically motivated, and experimentally robust contribution to AI-driven scientific discovery. The combination of objective programmatic benchmarks, rigorous baseline comparisons, comprehensive ablations, and blinded human expert validation meets the standard for curated acceptance.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The work acknowledges computational requirements of running verified code evaluations, reliance on small dense models for V-usable information estimation, and dependence on LLMs for semantic grouping during large-scale scoring.
